metrics.name: follow_up_questions
metrics.title: Follow-up questions
metrics.evidence: Many questions could only follow reading the output, e.g. #86-88 on what TYPES and frozenset do and whether to rename TYPES, #99-101 on the TypeAdapter and json.loads with isinstance, #46 on normalising nct_id, and #55 on BlankAsNone.

metrics.name: coding_guidelines
metrics.title: Coding guidelines
metrics.evidence: Every guideline that applied to the Python tools change (global CLAUDE.md, coding, git and Python rules, and the project and backend CLAUDE.md files) was in context, and all nine commit subjects follow the required form (lowercase, under 50 characters, no full stop, 'tools' scope, e.g. 'feat(tools): add ec trial parser'). The only unread files listed are node_modules CONTRIBUTING.md files, which do not apply to this change. I did not read the diff itself, so compliance beyond the commit subjects is not checked.

metrics.name: output_amendments
metrics.title: Output amendments
metrics.evidence: 316 of 2319 generated lines were rewritten after the author challenged them

metrics.name: prompt_granularity
metrics.title: Prompt granularity
metrics.evidence: Median generated lines per producing prompt was 26 (32 of 113 prompts produced output), and the work moved in stepwise approvals (plan-issue, then repeated 'y' and small corrections), though a few prompts such as the 312-line 'Yes' and the 178-line one exceeded 200 lines.
